DISPUTED with a specific, checkable error, same rigor as the Utah case. Original notes claimed: 'Extensive manual Commons search found only the university's logo ... no real campus building photograph exists in Commons under any of UNIFESP's six campus names.' I queried the Wikimedia Commons API directly (action=query&list=categorymembers on Category:Universidade_Federal_de_Sao_Paulo) and got 47 files back, the large majority of which are genuine campus building photographs, not the logo. I downloaded and viewed two at full resolution to confirm they are real: (1) 'Campus Sao Paulo da Unifesp.jpg' (3860x2573, CC BY-SA 4.0, attributed Alex Reipert) shows a building facade with 'UNIVERSIDADE FEDERAL DE SAO PAULO' and 'ESCOLA PAULISTA DE MEDICINA' carved in large letters directly on the building itself -- about the strongest possible correct-entity signal. (2) 'Reitoria da UNIFESP em 2025.jpg' (4004x3468, CC BY 4.0, Boaventuravinicius, dated 2025) shows another building with 'UNIFESP' lettering visible on it. The category also contains named, dedicated files for every one of the six campuses the original notes said were searched and came up empty: Campus Baixada Santista, Campus Diadema, Campus Osasco (three variant files), Campus Sao Paulo, Campus Zona Leste, Campus Sao Jose dos Campos (ICT-Unifesp) -- plus Unifesp Vila Clementino, Unifesp - Campus Guarulhos, several Hospital Sao Paulo / Hemocentro files, and eight numbered historical 'Escola Paulista de Medicina' photos. This is a real, significant miss, not a close call: multiple large, clearly-licensed, well-attributed, unambiguously-identified campus photos were sitting in the exact category the original search says it checked. Recommend re-running the source task for this row using 'Campus Sao Paulo da Unifesp.jpg' or 'Reitoria da UNIFESP em 2025.jpg' as the candidate.

Checked the Commons category myself. Found one file the original notes did not mention: 'INTI Subang - Mapillary (FrFeVDhUppVU9dh1EVMB5W).jpg', 1956x1100, CC BY-SA 4.0, dated 2020, described as 'INTI Subang' -- large enough to pass validation, unlike the two small files that were mentioned. However, I verified via web search that 'INTI International University' specifically and only refers to the Nilai (Negeri Sembilan) campus as the accredited university entity; Subang Jaya, Penang, and Sabah are officially branded 'INTI International College' -- a related but legally/formally distinct tier within the same corporate group. So this Subang file has exactly the same wrong-specific-campus problem the original notes correctly flagged for the Penang photo -- it doesn't change the outcome. Genuine gap confirmed, though the original file inventory undercounted (said 'the only large one' when there were in fact two large-but-wrong-campus candidates).

Viewed directly, no text/signage visible in frame so I cross-checked the architecture against independent sources. It's an 8-story modernist high-rise with an angled, boat-like beveled roofline and an irregular grid of colored glass panels (blue/grey, with yellow and red accent panels), aluminum-framed ribbon windows. Web search independently confirms UFMG's landmark Reitoria (Rectory) building on the Pampulha campus, built 1962 by architect Eduardo Mendes Guimaraes Junior, is specifically described as an 8-story free-plan modernist building with a 'boat-like beveled' shape and independent aluminum/glass ribbon-window facade -- a strong architectural match. Combined with the wikimedia_verified sourcing and named CC BY-SA 4.0 attribution (Galabel Morea), I'm confident this is genuinely UFMG's building. Confirmed.
